items.title: Beach Clean-up
items.text: Dear members, I am writing about next Saturday's beach clean-up. Last month only twelve people came, and the shore was still covered with plastic bottles and bags. We hope more of you can join us this time. Gloves and bags will be provided, but please bring your own water and a hat, because there is little shade. If it rains, we will move the event to the following Saturday. Please reply by Wednesday so that we can order enough supplies. Thank you for caring about our town. Mina, Green Club

qs.q: Why did Mina write this email?
o: To report the result of last month's event
To ask members to join an event and reply
To explain how to recycle plastic at home
To announce that the club will be closed
qs.why: 참여를 부탁하고 수요일까지 답장해 달라고 요청하는 글이에요.

qs.q: Why does Mina mention that only twelve people came last month?
o: Because more helpers are needed this time
Because the beach was already clean
Because the weather was too hot on that day
Because twelve is the number of gloves
qs.why: 지난달 참가자가 적어 해변이 여전히 지저분했다는 점에서 더 많은 도움이 필요하다는 것을 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: The word "provided" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: provided는 '제공된'이라는 뜻으로 supplied와 가까워요.

qs.q: What can we infer about the beach?
o: It is closed on rainy days only
It is far from the town center and hard to reach
There is not much place to stay out of the sun
It has a lot of tall trees
qs.why: little shade라고 했으므로 그늘이 별로 없다고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: What will happen if it rains next Saturday?
o: The members will stay and wait for the sun
The clean-up will be held a week later
The club will order more supplies
Only twelve people will be asked to come
qs.why: 비가 오면 그다음 토요일로 옮긴다고 했어요.

items.title: Library Notice
items.text: Attention, students. The school library will close at 3:00 p.m. every day this week because workers are repairing the roof. The noise during the repair is too loud for reading, and some shelves must be covered. Books can still be returned through the box beside the main door, and no late fees will be charged until Monday. If you need a book for your project, please ask Ms. Park in the office before noon. We are sorry for the trouble and thank you for your patience.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this notice?
o: To tell students about a temporary change
To ask students to buy new books
To praise the workers for their effort
To introduce a new library teacher
qs.why: 도서관이 일시적으로 일찍 닫는다는 변경 사항을 알리는 글이에요.

qs.q: Why will late fees not be charged until Monday?
o: Because the library will have no books to lend
Because Ms. Park is on vacation
Because the roof was fixed last Friday
Because returning books is harder this week
qs.why: 수리 때문에 반납이 불편하므로 연체료를 면제해 주는 거예요.

qs.q: The phrase "thank you for your patience" shows that the writer
o: expects students to feel a little upset
is planning a surprise party for the school
qs.why: 불편을 끼쳐 미안하다는 뜻이며, 학생들이 조금 불편해할 것을 예상해요.

qs.q: What should a student do to get a book for a project?
o: Use the box beside the main door
Talk to Ms. Park before twelve
Wait until the roof is repaired
qs.why: 정오 전에 사무실의 Ms. Park에게 요청하라고 했어요.

items.title: Before the Recital
items.text: Saturday, October 3. I could not eat breakfast today. My hands felt cold, and I kept playing the same four bars again and again. Mom said, "You know this piece better than anyone." I smiled, but my stomach did not agree. In the hall, I looked at the big black piano and wished I could walk home. Then Mr. Han gave me a thumbs-up from the first row. My fingers were still shaking when I sat down, but when the first note came out clean, I finally took a breath.

qs.q: How did the writer feel before the recital?
qs.why: 아침도 못 먹고 손이 차갑다고 했으므로 긴장한 상태예요.

qs.q: What does "my stomach did not agree" mean?
o: The writer had a serious illness
The writer was still nervous inside
qs.why: 웃었지만 속으로는 여전히 긴장하고 있다는 함축적 표현이에요.

qs.q: Why did the writer feel better at the end?
o: Mom sat in the first row
The piano was smaller than expected
The opening note was played well
qs.why: 첫 음을 깔끔하게 치자 마침내 숨을 쉬었다고 했어요.

qs.q: Who is Mr. Han most likely to be?
qs.why: 객석에서 엄지를 들어 격려한 것으로 보아 선생님일 가능성이 가장 커요.

items.title: Cooking for Beginners
items.text: Have you ever burned toast? Don't worry! Our Saturday morning cooking class is made for people who have never held a knife. In four weeks, you will learn to cook six simple meals, from vegetable soup to fried rice. Each class has only eight students, so the teacher can help everyone. All food is shared at the end of class, and you can take the recipes home. The first lesson is free. Sign up at the front desk of Hillside Community Center before the end of this month.

qs.q: What is the writer's main purpose?
o: To get people to join a class
To teach how to make soup
To warn people about kitchen knives
To report a cooking contest result
qs.why: 광고의 목적은 수업 등록을 유도하는 거예요.

qs.q: Why does the writer ask, "Have you ever burned toast?"
o: To complain about a broken toaster
To sell a new kind of bread
To test how well the readers can cook at home
To show the class is friendly to beginners
qs.why: 서툰 사람도 환영한다는 분위기를 만들기 위한 질문이에요.

qs.q: Why does the class have only eight students?
o: So that the food can be sold
Because the kitchen has no tables
So that each person can get help
Because the teacher is a beginner
qs.why: 선생님이 모두를 도울 수 있도록 인원을 제한한 거예요.

qs.q: Which is true about the first lesson?
o: It is held on a Sunday
qs.why: 첫 수업은 무료(free)라고 했어요.

items.title: A Week Without Phones
items.text: Last month my family tried an experiment: no phones at dinner. At first, it felt strange. My brother kept looking at the empty place beside his plate, and Dad did not know what to do with his hands. By the third night, though, we were talking about everything: school, Grandma's garden, even our silly dreams. I am not saying phones are bad. But I realized that I had not heard my father laugh like that in a long time. Maybe the best conversations start when nothing is buzzing.

qs.q: What is the writer's opinion?
o: Putting phones away can improve family time
Dinner should be eaten quickly and in silence
Grandma's garden is the best topic
qs.why: 휴대폰을 치우면 대화가 풍부해진다는 것이 필자의 생각이에요.

qs.q: Why did Dad "not know what to do with his hands"?
o: He wanted to leave the table
He was too tired to eat
He was used to holding his phone
qs.why: 평소 휴대폰을 들고 있던 습관 때문에 손이 어색했던 거예요.

qs.q: What can we infer from "I am not saying phones are bad"?
o: The writer bought a new phone
The writer lost his phone on a recent trip
The writer wants to avoid a one-sided view
qs.why: 휴대폰을 무조건 비난하지 않으려는 균형 잡힌 태도예요.

qs.q: What does the last sentence suggest?
o: Buzzing is a type of music at dinner
qs.why: 아무것도 울리지 않을 때 좋은 대화가 시작된다는 의미예요.

items.title: A Cold Bowl of Soup
items.text: To the manager of Blue Door Restaurant, I visited your restaurant last Friday for my mother's birthday. We waited forty minutes for our food, and the soup arrived cold. When we told the waiter, he only said, "The kitchen is busy." I understand that Fridays are hard, and the dessert was delicious. However, a birthday dinner should not feel like a test of patience. I hope you will train your staff to respond more kindly. I would like to visit again, and I hope the next experience will be better. Sincerely, Hana Kim

qs.q: Why did Hana write this letter?
o: To complain about the service she received
To book a table for her mother
To ask for a job at the restaurant
To thank the manager for dessert
qs.why: 서비스에 대한 불만을 전달하는 항의 편지예요.

qs.q: How would you describe the tone of the letter?
qs.why: 공손하지만 실망한 어조가 드러나요.

qs.q: What does the writer mean by "a test of patience"?
o: The restaurant gave a quiz to each table
The waiting was too long to enjoy
The dessert was hard to eat
qs.why: 오래 기다리는 것이 인내심 시험 같았다는 비유예요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about Hana?
o: She will never visit the place again
She may come back if things improve
She often eats there on Fridays
She works in the kitchen herself
qs.why: 다음에는 더 좋기를 바라며 다시 방문하고 싶다고 했어요.

items.title: Biscuit Comes Home
items.text: When Biscuit did not come home for dinner, Ben's chest felt tight. He walked up and down the street, calling the dog's name until his voice was rough. Mrs. Lopez from next door opened her window. "I heard a noise in my garden shed this afternoon," she said. Ben ran there, pulled the door open, and found Biscuit asleep on a pile of old blankets, with a half-eaten bone beside him. Ben laughed so hard that he sat down on the grass. Then he hugged the dog and said, "Next time, please tell me where you are going."

qs.q: How did Ben feel at the beginning?
qs.why: 가슴이 조이는 느낌이라고 했으므로 걱정스러운 상태예요.

qs.q: Why did Ben laugh when he found Biscuit?
o: He thought the shed was funny
He was angry at Mrs. Lopez
qs.why: 안심되고 우스꽝스러운 상황이라 웃음이 터진 거예요.

qs.q: What can we infer about Biscuit?
o: He ran away from home forever
He was hurt by a loud noise
He had been eating and sleeping in the shed
qs.why: 뼈다귀를 먹다 만 채 담요 위에서 자고 있었어요.

qs.q: The expression "his voice was rough" suggests that Ben
o: had called out for a long time
was singing a song to the neighbors
qs.why: 오래 불러서 목소리가 쉬었다는 뜻이에요.

items.title: Later School Mornings
items.text: Many teenagers feel tired at school because their bodies naturally want to sleep later at night and wake up later in the morning. Researchers say this change in the body clock is normal at this age. In one town, a school moved its first class from 8:00 to 9:00. After a year, students were late less often, and many said they paid more attention in class. Of course, a later start also means a later finish, which may be difficult for sports teams. Still, the results suggest that a small change can make a big difference.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: A later start time may help students
Teenagers should sleep during classes at school
Schools should have no first class
qs.why: 등교 시간이 늦춰지면 학생들에게 도움이 될 수 있다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: Why do teenagers feel sleepy in the morning?
o: They wake up for sports teams
qs.why: 청소년기에는 체내 시계가 늦어진다고 했어요.

qs.q: The phrase "a small change can make a big difference" refers to
o: taking a year off from school
moving the class start by one hour
qs.why: 한 시간 늦춘 것이 큰 차이를 만들었다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is mentioned as a possible problem?
o: Students might be late more often
Sports teams may have trouble with time
Teachers will lose their classrooms in the morning
Parents will have to drive more
qs.why: 늦게 끝나면 운동부에 어려움이 있을 수 있다고 했어요.

items.title: Not What I Expected
items.text: I almost did not go to see the new animated film. The poster looked childish, and my friends said it was only about a talking turtle. I expected to check my watch every ten minutes. Instead, I found myself holding my breath during the storm scene, and I was surprised to feel sad when the turtle said goodbye to his friends. The jokes are clever enough for adults, too. The only weak part is the ending, which feels a little rushed. If you like stories about friendship, give this one a chance.

qs.q: What is the writer's overall opinion of the film?
o: Better than expected, with a small weakness
Perfect in every way, without any problems at all
qs.why: 기대보다 훨씬 좋았지만 결말이 서두른 느낌이라고 했어요.

qs.q: Why did the writer expect to "check my watch every ten minutes"?
o: He had to catch a bus soon
He was waiting for a friend
He liked to count the minutes
He thought the film would be dull
qs.why: 지루할 거라 예상했다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which scene made the writer hold his breath?
qs.why: 폭풍 장면에서 숨을 죽였다고 했어요.

qs.q: Who is the passage mainly written for?
o: People who make animated films for a living
qs.why: 마지막 문장이 우정 이야기를 좋아하는 사람에게 권하고 있어요.

items.title: Vote for Daniel
items.text: Hello, everyone. My name is Daniel, and I want to be your student council president. Some people ask, "What can one student change?" Last spring, I asked for a bike rack near the gate, and now thirty bikes are parked there every day. If I win, I will ask the school to open the gym for free play on rainy lunch breaks, and I will start a book swap on the first Friday of each month. I cannot promise that everything will be easy. But I promise to listen, and I promise to try. Thank you.

qs.q: What is the speaker's main purpose?
o: To persuade students to vote for him
To say goodbye to his classmates and teachers
To report on a school event
qs.why: 학생회장 선거 연설로, 표를 얻기 위한 글이에요.

qs.q: Why does Daniel mention the bike rack?
o: To show he is good at sports
To prove that he can make real changes
qs.why: 자전거 보관대 사례는 자신의 실행력을 보여 주는 근거예요.

qs.q: What does "I cannot promise that everything will be easy" suggest?
o: Daniel dislikes hard work and long meetings
Daniel is honest about the challenges
qs.why: 쉽지 않을 것을 인정하는 솔직한 태도를 보여 줘요.

qs.q: When will the book swap take place?
qs.why: 매월 첫 금요일이라고 했으므로 한 달에 한 번이에요.

items.title: Caring for a Cactus
items.text: Many people believe a cactus needs almost no care, but this idea can actually kill the plant. First, put it by a bright window, because it needs at least four hours of sunlight. Second, water it only when the soil is completely dry, usually every two or three weeks. Too much water makes the roots rot, which is the most common reason cacti die. Finally, use a pot with holes in the bottom so that extra water can escape. Follow these steps, and your cactus may live for many years.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
o: To explain how to keep a cactus healthy
To argue that cacti are dangerous to keep at home
qs.why: 선인장 관리 방법을 설명하는 글이에요.

qs.q: What can we infer about watering a cactus?
o: It needs water every single day
Cold water is worse than warm water
Giving it too much water is harmful
qs.why: 과습이 뿌리를 썩게 해 가장 흔한 사망 원인이라고 했어요.

qs.q: Why should the pot have holes in the bottom?
o: To give the roots more sunlight
To keep insects out of the soil
To let extra water drain out
qs.why: 남는 물이 빠져나가도록 하기 위해서예요.

qs.q: The word "rot" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: rot은 '썩다'라는 뜻으로 decay와 가까워요.

items.title: Where Have the Bees Gone?
items.text: In some parts of the world, farmers have noticed that fewer bees are visiting their fields. This matters because bees carry pollen from flower to flower, and many fruits and vegetables cannot grow without it. Scientists believe that several things are to blame, including strong chemicals, disease, and the loss of wild flowers. Some towns have begun planting gardens for bees along roads and on roofs. One researcher said, "If we help the bees, we are really helping ourselves." It is a reminder that small animals can have a huge effect on our meals.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why bees matter to human food
How to build a honey farm
qs.why: 벌이 줄어드는 문제와 그것이 식량에 주는 영향을 다뤄요.

qs.q: What does the researcher mean by "we are really helping ourselves"?
o: Bees will give us free honey
Researchers need more money to study bees
Protecting bees also protects our food
qs.why: 벌을 돕는 것이 곧 우리의 식량을 지키는 일이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Which is NOT given as a cause of the problem?
o: Strong chemicals used on farm fields
Too many farmers planting wild flowers
qs.why: 야생화 감소가 원인이지 야생화를 심는 것이 원인은 아니에요.

qs.q: What does the writer want readers to realize?
o: Bees are more important than all fruit and vegetables
Small animals can greatly affect daily life
Roads should be closed to cars
qs.why: 작은 동물이 우리 식탁에 큰 영향을 준다는 점이에요.

items.title: The Missed Train
items.text: Yuri watched the last train leave the platform just as she reached the stairs. It was already nine o'clock, her phone battery was at two percent, and she had never been in this city alone. A young man in a blue jacket noticed her worried face. "Where do you need to go?" he asked. After she explained, he showed her the way to a night bus and even waited with her until it came. When she tried to thank him, he only shrugged and said, "Someone did the same for me once." On the bus, Yuri decided she would pass that kindness on.

qs.q: What problem did Yuri have at the start?
o: She had missed the final train
She had forgotten the city's name
She had no money for a ticket
qs.why: 막차를 놓쳤어요.

qs.q: What does "Someone did the same for me once" suggest about the young man?
o: He works for the train company
He is a friend of the family of Yuri's mother
He once received similar help himself
qs.why: 예전에 누군가 자신을 도와준 적이 있다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How did Yuri most likely feel at the end?
qs.why: 친절을 다른 사람에게도 전하겠다고 결심했으므로 감사하며 감동한 상태예요.

qs.q: Why is her phone battery mentioned?
o: It explains why the night bus was so late
It shows how hard it was to get help
It proves the man was rich
It tells us the train's price
qs.why: 배터리가 거의 없어서 혼자 해결하기 어려운 상황이었음을 강조해요.

items.title: A Request for More Time
items.text: Dear Mr. Kim, I am sorry to bother you. I am writing about the science report due this Friday. I have finished the experiment, but last week I had a bad flu and missed three days of school, so I have not been able to write the conclusion. I think I need two more days to do it properly. I understand that this is a lot to ask, and I will accept a lower score if you think it is fair. I would be very grateful for your understanding. Thank you for your time. Sincerely, Jiho Park

qs.q: Why did Jiho write this email?
o: To ask for an extension on a report
To complain about a low score
To report that he is sick again today
To invite Mr. Kim to his lab
qs.why: 마감 연장을 부탁하는 이메일이에요.

qs.q: What is the reason for his request?
o: Illness caused him to miss school
qs.why: 독감으로 사흘 결석했다고 했어요.

qs.q: What does the sentence "I will accept a lower score" show about Jiho?
o: He does not care about science
He wants to quit the class
He is willing to take responsibility
He thinks the teacher is being unfair to him
qs.why: 더 낮은 점수도 받아들이겠다는 것은 책임을 지려는 태도예요.

qs.q: What is the tone of the email?
qs.why: 정중하고 미안해하는 어조예요.

items.title: Flea Market for Paws
items.text: Come to the Oakwood Flea Market this Sunday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.! Neighbors will sell books, toys, plants, and homemade snacks. Every dollar earned at the red tables goes to Safe Paws, a small shelter that takes care of stray dogs and cats. Last year, our market paid for winter blankets for forty animals. If you have items to donate, drop them off at the school gym on Saturday morning. Bring a bag, bring a friend, and, if you cannot find anything to buy, you can still help by saying hello to the volunteers.

qs.q: What is the purpose of this poster?
o: To invite people to a charity event
To advertise a new pet shop
To warn people about stray dogs
qs.why: 동물 보호소를 돕는 자선 행사에 초대하는 포스터예요.

qs.q: What happens to the money from the red tables?
o: It pays for the school gym
It is divided among the sellers
It buys snacks for the volunteers
It supports a shelter for animals
qs.why: 빨간 테이블의 수익은 Safe Paws에 기부돼요.

qs.q: Why does the poster mention last year's blankets?
o: To say that winter has already started
To show how the money was used
qs.why: 지난해 수익이 어떻게 쓰였는지 보여 주는 예시예요.

qs.q: What can we infer from the last sentence?
o: Visitors are welcome even if they buy nothing
The market will close early if no one buys things
qs.why: 아무것도 사지 않아도 인사만으로 도울 수 있다고 하니 방문 자체가 환영받아요.

items.title: Grandma's Sewing Machine
items.text: In the corner of Grandma's room sits an old sewing machine with a black body and a gold flower on its side. When I was small, I thought it was a sleeping animal. Grandma used it to make every school bag I ever carried. Last winter, her hands became too weak to sew, and the machine fell silent. Yesterday I found a piece of cloth in the drawer and asked her to show me how to start. She laughed, put her wrinkled hand over mine, and said, "Slowly, slowly. The machine will tell you what it wants."

qs.q: What does the sentence "the machine fell silent" mean?
o: The machine made a strange noise
qs.why: 할머니가 더 이상 재봉틀을 쓰지 않게 되었다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why did the writer think it was a "sleeping animal"?
o: It was kept in the garden
Grandma named it after a pet
The writer was a small child then
qs.why: 어렸을 때의 상상이었다는 것이 맥락이에요.

qs.q: What does the scene at the end suggest?
o: Grandma wants to sell the machine
A skill is being passed to a new generation
The cloth in the drawer was brand new and clean
qs.why: 할머니가 손녀 손을 잡고 가르치며 기술이 이어지는 장면이에요.

qs.q: What feeling is shown between the two people?
qs.why: 웃으며 손을 포개는 모습에서 따뜻한 애정이 느껴져요.

items.title: Bike Sharing Comes to Town
items.text: Since spring, red bicycles have appeared at forty stations around our city. You scan a code with your phone, ride for as long as you like, and leave the bike at any station. The first thirty minutes cost nothing, and after that, a small fee is charged. The city says that more than ten thousand trips are taken each week. Not everyone is happy, though. Some shop owners complain that bikes are left on the sidewalk, and older residents say the roads are not safe enough. The city has promised to add bike lanes next year.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A new bike program and reactions to it
How to repair a red bicycle
A race held in the city center
qs.why: 자전거 공유 서비스와 그에 대한 반응을 다뤄요.

qs.q: What can be inferred from "The city has promised to add bike lanes next year"?
o: Cars will be banned from the city roads soon
Safety concerns are being taken seriously
qs.why: 시가 안전 우려에 대응하려 한다는 것을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: When must a rider pay?
o: When leaving the bike at the next station
After using a bike for half an hour
qs.why: 처음 30분은 무료이고 이후에 요금이 부과돼요.

qs.q: Who is unhappy with the program?
o: Some shop owners and older residents
qs.why: 상점 주인과 노인 주민들이 불만을 제기했어요.

items.title: After the Final Whistle
items.text: The match ended 3-1, and our team had lost its first game of the season. Nobody spoke in the locker room. Coach Reyes waited until everyone had taken off their shoes. "I am not going to say that losing is fine," she began. "But I watched the second half, and I saw ten players running for each other. That is what I came here to see." She smiled for the first time that day. "Tonight, rest. Tomorrow, we begin to fix the passing. Understood?" A few of us laughed, and the room felt a little lighter.

qs.q: What is the coach's purpose in speaking to the team?
o: To encourage the players after a loss
To blame them for the defeat
To announce a change of schedule for the week
qs.why: 패배한 선수들을 격려하기 위한 말이에요.

qs.q: Why did the coach wait before she spoke?
o: She was waiting for the referee to come back
She wanted the players to settle down first
qs.why: 신발을 벗고 진정할 때까지 기다린 거예요.

qs.q: What does "the room felt a little lighter" mean?
qs.why: 분위기가 한결 가벼워졌다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does the coach want to improve next?
qs.why: 내일 패스를 고치기 시작하겠다고 했어요.

items.title: Burnt Pancakes
items.text: My first attempt at making pancakes for the family ended in smoke. I turned the heat too high, and the outsides turned black while the insides were still wet. My sister took one bite, made a face, and politely said, "Interesting." Dad, however, ate two and called them "crunchy." The second time, I used a lower heat and a timer, and the pancakes came out golden. I have learned that cooking is a lot like many other things: you rarely get it right the first time, and a good laugh helps you try again.

qs.q: What is the tone of the passage?
qs.why: 실패를 웃음으로 넘기는 유쾌하고 긍정적인 글이에요.

qs.q: What did the sister's word "Interesting" really mean?
o: She liked the black color a lot
She did not enjoy the taste
qs.why: 표정을 찌푸리며 예의상 한 말이므로 맛이 없었다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why were the first pancakes ruined?
o: The heat was set too high
qs.why: 불이 너무 세서 겉만 타고 속은 덜 익었어요.

qs.q: What lesson does the writer draw?
o: Mistakes are a normal part of learning
qs.why: 처음부터 잘하기 어렵고 웃으며 다시 시도하는 게 중요하다는 교훈이에요.

items.title: Parking Rules
items.text: Notice to all residents of Maple Court: Beginning on the first of next month, cars may be parked only in marked spaces. Vehicles left in front of the fire exits or in the playground area will be removed at the owner's cost. Each household may register two cars. Visitors can use the blue spaces near the gate for up to four hours. We know that parking has become difficult since the new shop opened, but safety must come first. Please read the new map outside the management office, and contact us if you have any questions.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this notice?
o: To ask for help in the playground
To invite neighbors to a meeting
qs.why: 새 주차 규정을 알리는 공지예요.

qs.q: Why are cars not allowed in front of fire exits?
o: Because the map is outside the office
Because safety is the first concern
qs.why: 안전이 최우선이라는 말에서 이유를 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What can we infer from "parking has become difficult since the new shop opened"?
o: The residents moved away last month
More cars are coming into the area
qs.why: 새 가게가 생긴 뒤 차가 많아졌음을 짐작할 수 있어요.

qs.q: How long can a visitor use a blue space?
qs.why: 방문객은 최대 4시간까지 쓸 수 있어요.

items.title: Letter from a Pen Pal
items.text: Dear Sam, Winter has finally arrived here in Sapporo, and the whole town is white. Last weekend, my class went to the snow festival. Teams from every school built huge snow statues, and at night, lights made them glow like glass. My favorite one was a dragon almost as tall as a house. We drank hot corn soup to keep warm, and my fingers were so cold that I could not hold my pen to take notes! I wish you could see it for yourself. Please write soon and tell me about winter in your country. Your friend, Aiko

qs.q: Why did Aiko write this letter?
o: To share her experience and invite a reply
To ask Sam for a loan
To announce a trip to Sam's country this winter
qs.why: 경험을 나누고 답장을 요청하는 편지예요.

qs.q: What does "the whole town is white" mean?
qs.why: 눈이 마을을 덮었다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why could Aiko not take notes at the festival?
o: She forgot to bring a notebook
The statues were too far away
Her fingers were too cold to hold a pen
qs.why: 손가락이 너무 시려 펜을 잡을 수 없었어요.

qs.q: What does "I wish you could see it for yourself" show?
o: Aiko plans to visit Sam in his country soon
Aiko wants to share the moment with Sam
Aiko is sad about the festival
Sam has seen the festival before
qs.why: 그 광경을 함께 보고 싶은 마음을 표현해요.

items.title: Paper or Screen?
items.text: Many students now read on tablets and phones, but some studies suggest that paper may be better for deep reading. In one experiment, students who read a long story on paper remembered the order of events more clearly than those who read it on a screen. Researchers think this is because it is easier to feel the length of a book and to flip back to earlier pages. However, the same studies found that screens are useful for short texts and quick searches. The best choice probably depends on what you are reading and why you are reading it.

qs.q: Which sentence best expresses the writer's view?
o: Each type of reading has its own best use
Tablets are always better than paper books
qs.why: 읽는 목적과 종류에 따라 최선이 달라진다는 결론이에요.

qs.q: The word "suggest" in the first sentence is closest to
qs.why: suggest는 '시사하다'로 indicate와 가까워요.

qs.q: What is one reason paper may help memory?
o: Paper makes the pages louder when readers turn them
Readers can feel how far they are in the book
qs.why: 분량을 몸으로 느끼고 앞 페이지로 쉽게 넘길 수 있기 때문이에요.

qs.q: When are screens described as useful?
o: For quick searches and short texts
For reading in a bright garden or park
qs.why: 짧은 글과 빠른 검색에는 화면이 유용하다고 했어요.

items.title: The Volcano That Would Not Erupt
items.text: Nari had worked on her science fair volcano for two weeks. She had painted the sides brown and gray and made a tiny village at the bottom. When the judges arrived, she poured in the baking soda and vinegar, but only a few bubbles crept out. Her face turned hot. Then one of the judges smiled and said, "I like that you put a village there. Tell me, what do you think went wrong?" Nari took a breath and explained that she had measured the baking soda by eye. Afterward, she wrote in her notebook: "Measure first, wonder later."

qs.q: How did Nari feel when the volcano failed?
qs.why: 얼굴이 화끈거린다는 표현에서 당황한 마음을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: Why did the judge ask what went wrong?
o: To decide whether Nari made the village herself
To see if Nari could learn from the mistake
qs.why: 실패 원인을 스스로 설명하게 하는 것은 배움을 확인하려는 의도예요.

qs.q: What was the real cause of the problem?
o: The village was too heavy for the volcano
The baking soda was not measured exactly
qs.why: 눈대중으로 재서 양이 정확하지 않았어요.

qs.q: What does Nari's note suggest she learned?
qs.why: 먼저 정확히 재라는 교훈이에요.

items.title: A Thank-You Note
items.text: Dear volunteers, On behalf of the whole Riverside Care Home, I want to thank all twenty of you for last Saturday. When you arrived with your guitars and board games, I saw faces that I had not seen smile in weeks. Mr. Oh, who rarely speaks, even taught one of you to play a card game from his childhood. Your visit did more than fill an afternoon; it reminded our residents that they are not forgotten. We hope you will come again in the spring. With warm regards, Ms. Evans, Activities Manager

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this letter?
o: To express thanks for a visit
To invite people to work full-time
qs.why: 방문 봉사에 대한 감사 편지예요.

qs.q: What does "they are not forgotten" suggest about the residents?
qs.why: 잊히지 않았다고 상기시켜 주었다는 말은 외로움을 느낄 수 있음을 뜻해요.

qs.q: Why is the story about Mr. Oh included?
o: It explains why cards are banned there
It shows how much the visit meant
qs.why: 평소 말이 적은 분이 먼저 나선 사례는 방문의 의미를 보여 줘요.

qs.q: What does the writer hope will happen?
o: The care home will be much larger soon
qs.why: 봄에 다시 오기를 바란다고 했어요.

items.title: The Quiet Kettle
items.text: Introducing the Calm Kettle, the first electric kettle that boils water without a single whistle. Its soft blue light slowly fades from bright to dark as the water heats, so you can read, study, or simply think while you wait. A safety switch turns the kettle off by itself when the water is ready, and the handle stays cool to the touch. Whether you are a student studying late at night or a parent with a sleeping baby, you will never have to say "shh" to your tea again. Available in white, gray, and green.

qs.q: What is the main purpose of this text?
o: To persuade readers to buy a product
To teach how to make tea
qs.why: 제품을 소개해 구매를 유도하는 광고예요.

qs.q: Who would be the most likely customer?
o: Someone who never drinks tea or coffee
Someone who needs a quiet room
qs.why: 소음이 없다는 점이 강조된 광고예요.

qs.q: What does "you will never have to say 'shh' to your tea" mean?
o: The tea will be too hot to drink right away
Tea must be kept in silence
The kettle will not make disturbing noise
The kettle talks to the user
qs.why: 주전자 소리가 방해되지 않는다는 재치 있는 표현이에요.

qs.q: What does the safety switch do?
o: It turns the kettle off when water is ready
It locks the handle at night
qs.why: 물이 끓으면 스스로 꺼져요.

items.title: Sleep and the Teenage Brain
items.text: Many teenagers believe that staying up late to study will help them do well on a test. In fact, the opposite is often true. During sleep, the brain moves new information from short-term memory to long-term memory, so skipping sleep can make it harder to remember what you learned. A tired mind is also slower at solving problems and quicker to get upset. Experts recommend eight to ten hours of sleep for teenagers. Turning off screens an hour before bed and keeping the room dark are two easy ways to start.

qs.q: What is the writer's main message?
o: Enough sleep is important for learning
Studying at night is always the best way
Tests should be held at night
qs.why: 충분한 수면이 학습에 중요하다는 글이에요.

qs.q: What does "the opposite is often true" mean here?
o: Late studying always gives very high scores
Staying up late often hurts test results
qs.why: 밤샘이 오히려 시험에 도움이 되지 않는다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: According to the passage, what happens during sleep?
o: The body grows taller at once
The brain stores new information for later
qs.why: 수면 중 단기 기억이 장기 기억으로 옮겨져요.

qs.q: Which tip is given for better sleep?
qs.why: 방을 어둡게 하라는 팁이 있어요.

items.title: The Man with the Bread
items.text: Every afternoon at four o'clock, an old man sat on the same bench and opened a paper bag full of bread crumbs. Pigeons landed at his feet as if they had received an invitation. Eli, who passed the park on his way home, began to notice that the man never looked at his watch and never seemed to be waiting for anyone. One day, Eli stopped and said hello. The old man's face lit up. "I used to come here with my wife," he said, tossing a crumb. "Now these fellows keep me company."

qs.q: What can we infer about the old man?
o: He misses his wife and feels lonely
He sells bread to pigeons in the park
He works at the park office
qs.why: 아내와 함께 오곤 했고 지금은 새들이 동무라는 말에서 외로움을 알 수 있어요.

qs.q: What does "as if they had received an invitation" suggest about the pigeons?
o: They were angry at the man
qs.why: 초대받은 듯 자연스럽게 모여든다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why did the man's face "light up" when Eli spoke?
o: He wanted to sell the bench
He thought Eli was his son from long ago
He was glad to have someone to talk to
qs.why: 말 걸어 주는 사람이 있어 기뻤다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What is the meaning of "keep me company" in the last line?
o: stay with me so I am not alone
qs.why: keep company는 '곁에 있어 주다'라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: You Are Invited
items.text: Hi everyone! Mr. Lee is retiring after thirty-two years of teaching, and we are planning a party for him on Friday, June 12, at 4 p.m. in room 204. Please keep this a secret, because he thinks it will be a normal staff meeting! We are collecting messages and old photographs for a memory book, so please give yours to Sora by Wednesday. If you can bring a snack to share, that would be wonderful, but it is not required. Come with a big smile and a few good stories. See you there!

qs.q: Why is the writer sending this message?
o: To invite people to a surprise party
To announce a staff meeting for Friday
To ask Mr. Lee to retire
qs.why: 깜짝 파티 초대 글이에요.

qs.q: Why should people keep the party secret?
o: The party is on a school night
Mr. Lee does not know about it
qs.why: Mr. Lee는 평범한 직원 회의로 알고 있어요.

qs.q: What does "it is not required" mean about the snacks?
o: Only Sora and the teachers must bring snacks
Guests may choose whether to bring them
qs.why: 필수는 아니고 선택이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What should people give to Sora?
qs.why: 추억 책을 위한 메시지와 사진을 Sora에게 주라고 했어요.

items.title: Water at Our School
items.text: Last month, the Green Team measured how much water our school used each day. The biggest surprise was the school yard: sprinklers ran for an hour every morning, even on rainy days. The team also found three taps in the restrooms that dripped all day, wasting about 20 liters. Together, these two problems used more water than the cafeteria. The team recommends adding a rain sensor to the sprinklers and fixing the taps this month. If both changes are made, the school could save enough water to fill an entire swimming pool every year.

qs.q: What is the purpose of this report?
o: To suggest ways to save water
qs.why: 물 사용을 조사하고 절약 방안을 제안하는 보고서예요.

qs.q: What can we infer about the sprinklers?
o: They are controlled by students and teachers
They are used only on dry days
They are broken in every season
They do not respond to the weather
qs.why: 비 오는 날에도 켜진다고 했으므로 날씨에 반응하지 않아요.

qs.q: Which place used the most water, according to the passage?
o: The yard and restroom taps together
The teachers' room and the front hall
qs.why: 스프링클러와 수도꼭지 두 문제가 급식실보다 더 많이 썼어요.

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude to the problem?
qs.why: 해결책을 제시하며 기대하는 현실적이고 희망적인 태도예요.

items.title: My First Week at a New School
items.text: On Monday, I walked into a hallway full of strangers, and I felt like a fish in the wrong pond. Nobody was unkind, but nobody knew my name either. At lunch, I sat alone and pretended to be interested in my rice. On Wednesday, a girl named Hyeri asked if I liked drawing, because she had noticed the sketchbook in my bag. By Friday, we were sharing pencils and jokes. I still miss my old friends, but this school no longer feels like somebody else's home.

qs.q: What does "a fish in the wrong pond" mean?
o: The writer felt out of place
The writer was fond of swimming
The writer was lost in a park
The writer wanted to catch a fish
qs.why: 낯선 곳에서 어울리지 못하는 기분을 비유한 표현이에요.

qs.q: Why did the writer pretend to be interested in the rice?
qs.why: 혼자 있는 모습을 숨기려는 행동이에요.

qs.q: How did Hyeri start the conversation?
o: She introduced the teacher to the class
qs.why: 가방 속 스케치북을 보고 그림을 좋아하느냐고 물었어요.

qs.q: How does the writer feel by the end?
o: Ready to go back to the old school
More comfortable at the new school
qs.why: 더 이상 남의 집 같지 않다고 했어요.

items.title: The Baker's Day
items.text: Min-ho the baker gets up at 3 a.m. every day, long before the sun is up. By the time most people eat breakfast, he has already made two hundred loaves. "The first hour is the hardest," he says, wiping flour from his face. "After that, the smell of fresh bread wakes me up better than any coffee." He closes the shop at two in the afternoon, but his work does not end there; he must prepare the dough for tomorrow. When asked whether he gets tired, he laughs and says, "Only when the oven is cold."

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A baker's early and busy daily routine
How to make a perfect loaf
A bakery that is closing down this year
qs.why: 제빵사의 이른 하루 일과를 소개해요.

qs.q: What does the baker mean by "Only when the oven is cold"?
o: He feels energetic when he is busy baking
qs.why: 오븐이 따뜻하게 돌아갈 때, 즉 일할 때는 피곤하지 않다는 재치 있는 말이에요.

qs.q: When does Min-ho finish his work for the day?
o: After preparing dough for the next day
As soon as breakfast ends in the morning
qs.why: 문을 닫은 후에도 내일 반죽을 준비해야 하므로 그때 끝나요.

qs.q: What can we infer about Min-ho?
o: He wants to change jobs very soon
He takes pleasure in his job
qs.why: 빵 냄새가 커피보다 낫다며 웃는 모습에서 일을 즐긴다고 추론할 수 있어요.

items.title: Robots in the Hospital
items.text: In one hospital, a small robot now delivers medicine and meals to the rooms of patients. It rolls through the halls, stops politely at elevators, and says, "Excuse me," when people block its way. Nurses say that the robot saves them about two hours every day, which they can spend talking with patients. Some patients, however, miss seeing a human face at mealtime. The hospital plans to keep the robot but also ask nurses to say hello at each door. The goal is not to replace people but to give them more time to care.

qs.q: What is the main idea?
o: Robots can free nurses to spend time with people
Elevators in hospitals are too slow
qs.why: 로봇이 간호사의 시간을 아껴 환자 돌봄에 쓰게 한다는 내용이에요.

qs.q: Why do some patients feel uncomfortable?
o: The robot drops the medicine in the hall
They miss seeing a person during meals
qs.why: 식사 때 사람 얼굴을 보지 못해 아쉬워한다고 했어요.

qs.q: What does the last sentence suggest about the hospital's attitude?
o: Machines are better than nurses at caring
People should remain the center of care
qs.why: 목표가 사람을 대체하는 것이 아니라 더 돌볼 시간을 주는 것이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: The word "deliver" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: deliver는 '배달하다'로 bring과 가까워요.

items.title: More Benches, Please
items.text: To the editor: I walk through Central Park every morning, and I have noticed something worrying. There are only six benches along the main path, which is nearly two kilometers long. Last week, an elderly woman had to sit on a low stone wall to catch her breath. Parks are for everyone, not only for fast runners. I urge the city to add at least ten more benches, especially near the playground and the pond. Such a small investment would make a large difference to older visitors and to parents with small children. Yours truly, Henry Ross

qs.q: What is the writer's purpose?
o: To ask the city to take action
qs.why: 벤치를 더 설치해 달라고 시에 요구하는 글이에요.

qs.q: Why does he mention the elderly woman?
o: To give a real example of the problem
qs.why: 구체적 사례로 문제를 보여 주는 거예요.

qs.q: What does "Parks are for everyone, not only for fast runners" imply?
o: Parks need a faster path for runners
qs.why: 빠르지 않은 사람도 공원을 이용할 수 있어야 한다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: The phrase "a small investment" refers to
qs.why: 벤치를 늘리는 비용이 작은 투자라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: The Night of the Storm
items.text: The wind began to howl at dusk, and by midnight the little fishing village was shaking. Old Captain Roh checked the ropes on his boat for the third time and then went to the harbor bell. He rang it hard, again and again, so that everyone on the cliffs could hear. One by one, lights came on, and men and women hurried down to help move the boats. By dawn, the sea was calm. Not a single boat was lost. "A bell is just a piece of metal," the captain said with a tired smile. "It is the people who answer it."

qs.q: Why did Captain Roh ring the bell?
o: To wake the village so people could help
To announce the end of the storm
To call fish into the harbor
qs.why: 마을 사람들을 깨워 도움을 요청하려는 거예요.

qs.q: What does the captain's last sentence mean?
o: The storm was not serious for the fishing boats
Cooperation matters more than the tool itself
qs.why: 종이 아니라 응답하는 사람들이 중요하다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What can we infer about the village?
o: Its boats are all very old and small
Its people care for one another
Its harbor is in a big city
qs.why: 종소리에 사람들이 모여 함께 배를 옮겼어요.

qs.q: What happened by dawn?
qs.why: 새벽에는 바다가 잔잔해졌다고 했어요.

items.title: What Failure Teaches
items.text: Many people think of failure as the opposite of success, but it is often a step toward it. A gardener who grows nothing in the first year learns which soil is too dry. A runner who stops halfway learns how to pace herself. Even a scientist whose experiment fails gains useful information, because now she knows one more thing that does not work. Of course, failure is never fun. It stings, and it can make us want to quit. Yet those who keep trying and think carefully about each mistake are the ones who finally find a way forward.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Failure can be a useful part of learning
qs.why: 실패가 배움의 일부라는 내용이에요.

qs.q: Why does the writer say the scientist "gains useful information"?
o: She earns a lot of money from her experiment
She finds out one thing that does not work
qs.why: 실패한 방법 하나를 알게 되는 것도 정보라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: The word "stings" is used to show that failure
o: makes a loud sound that wakes people
causes a sharp feeling of pain
qs.why: stings는 마음이 따끔하게 아픈 느낌을 나타내요.

qs.q: What is the writer's attitude toward failure?
qs.why: 실패가 아프다는 것을 인정하면서도 격려해요.

items.title: Returning a Jacket
items.text:
Clerk: Hello. How can I help you?
Jin: Hi. I bought this jacket yesterday, but the zipper is stuck.
Clerk: I see. Do you have your receipt with you?
Jin: Yes, here it is. I'd like a refund, if possible.
Clerk: I'm afraid we can only give a refund within seven days, but that is no problem. It's only been one day.
Jin: Oh, good. Actually, I would prefer a different jacket in the same size.
Clerk: Of course. The blue one over there is the same price. Would you like to try it on?
Jin: Sure. And could you check that the zipper works before I leave?

qs.q: Why did Jin go to the shop?
o: To deal with a faulty jacket
To buy a present for a friend
qs.why: 지퍼가 고장 난 재킷 문제를 해결하러 갔어요.

qs.q: What does the clerk mean by "that is no problem"?
o: The shop is too busy today
The jacket cannot be returned after one day
The refund time limit is not an issue here
qs.why: 하루밖에 안 지나 7일 기한 내이므로 문제 없다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does Jin decide to do?
o: Take the money and leave the shop quickly
Exchange the jacket for another one
qs.why: 환불 대신 같은 사이즈의 다른 재킷을 원했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred from Jin's last question?
o: Jin does not like the blue color
Jin is careful not to make the same mistake
Jin has no time to try it on
qs.why: 새 재킷의 지퍼를 확인해 달라는 것은 같은 문제를 피하려는 신중함이에요.

items.title: Planning the Trip
items.text:
Eun: Have you decided where to go for our class trip?
Tom: Not yet. I like the science museum, but it is a bit expensive.
Eun: How about the mountain park? We could walk, and it's cheap.
Tom: That sounds nice, but the forecast says rain on Friday.
Eun: Oh, I didn't check. Then maybe the museum is a safer choice.
Tom: Right. If we ask everyone to bring a lunch, we can save money.
Eun: Good idea. I'll write a note for the class tonight.

qs.q: What problem do Eun and Tom face?
o: They are choosing between two possible places
They have lost the list of the whole class
They cannot find the science museum
qs.why: 비와 비용 때문에 장소를 고민하고 있어요.

qs.q: Why does Tom reject the mountain park?
o: It is too far from the school
Rain is expected on the day
qs.why: 금요일에 비 예보가 있기 때문이에요.

qs.q: What does Eun mean by "a safer choice"?
o: Cheaper than every other place on the list
Less likely to be spoiled by the weather
qs.why: 비가 와도 영향이 적다는 의미예요.

qs.q: What will Eun probably do next?
o: Write a note about bringing lunch
qs.why: 오늘 밤 학급에 알릴 쪽지를 쓰겠다고 했어요.

items.title: Asking for Advice
items.text:
Ms. Cho: Come in, Sara. You look worried.
Sara: I have been trying to write my essay, but I can't think of an ending.
Ms. Cho: Can you tell me what the essay is about?
Sara: It's about how my grandfather taught me to fish.
Ms. Cho: That's lovely. What did you learn from him besides fishing?
Sara: Well, patience, I suppose. He never got angry when I lost a fish.
Ms. Cho: There's your ending. Finish with what he really taught you.
Sara: Oh! I had been looking at the wrong part of the story. Thank you.

qs.q: Why did Sara visit Ms. Cho?
o: She needed help finishing her essay
She wanted to learn how to fish
She planned to change her topic again
qs.why: 에세이 결말을 짓지 못해 조언을 구하러 갔어요.

qs.q: What is Ms. Cho's advice?
o: Write about a different person in the family
End the essay with the lesson Sara learned
qs.why: 할아버지에게 배운 진짜 교훈으로 끝맺으라는 조언이에요.

qs.q: What does Sara mean by "the wrong part of the story"?
o: She was focusing on the wrong thing
qs.why: 결말을 엉뚱한 곳에서 찾고 있었다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: How does Sara feel at the end?
qs.why: 해결책을 찾아 안도하고 감사해요.

items.title: The Messy Room
items.text:
Mina: Joon, did you borrow my headphones again?
Joon: No. Why would I do that?
Mina: Because last week, you said you'd take them for a minute and kept them all weekend.
Joon: That was different. I gave them back, didn't I?
Mina: Only after I found them under your bed, next to a sock.
Joon: Okay, okay. Let me check my room.
Joon: Found them! They were behind the desk.
Mina: So you did borrow them.
Joon: Fine. Sorry. I'll ask next time.

qs.q: Why did Mina suspect Joon?
o: He had taken her headphones before
He had broken them last week at school
He was wearing them at home
qs.why: 지난주에 빌린 뒤 주말 내내 가져갔던 일이 있어서예요.

qs.q: What is the meaning of "That was different" in Joon's line?
o: He wants to buy new ones
He is trying to defend himself
qs.why: 자신을 변호하려는 말이에요.

qs.q: What can be inferred from the end of the conversation?
o: Mina found the headphones under her own bed
Joon did take the headphones this time
qs.why: 책상 뒤에서 찾았다는 것은 그가 가져간 것이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does Joon promise?
qs.why: 다음에는 먼저 묻겠다고 했어요.

items.title: A Lost Bag
items.text:
Staff: Airport lost-and-found. How can I help?
Ken: Hello, I flew in from Busan this morning, and I think I left my bag on the plane.
Staff: Can you describe it?
Ken: It's a small gray backpack with a red tag. There is a laptop inside.
Staff: Do you remember your seat number?
Ken: Yes, 14C. I put the bag under the seat in front of me.
Staff: Please hold on. I'll check with the cleaning crew.
Ken: Thank you. I have a presentation tomorrow, so this is really important.
Staff: A gray backpack with a red tag has just been found. You can pick it up at Gate 5 in thirty minutes.

qs.q: What is the purpose of Ken's call?
o: To find a bag he left behind
To book a flight to Busan
To complain about the cleaning crew
qs.why: 비행기에 두고 내린 가방을 찾으려는 전화예요.

qs.q: Why does Ken say "this is really important"?
o: He wants to sell the backpack
He is angry at the staff at the desk
He needs the laptop for tomorrow
qs.why: 내일 발표가 있기 때문이에요.

qs.q: Why does the staff member ask for a seat number?
o: To decide how much the bag is worth to Ken
To help the cleaning crew look in the right place
qs.why: 좌석 번호는 청소 팀이 정확한 위치를 찾게 도와줘요.

qs.q: What will Ken probably do next?
o: Fly back to Busan on the next plane
Go to Gate 5 and collect the bag
qs.why: 30분 뒤 5번 게이트에서 찾아가라고 안내받았어요.

items.title: Choosing a Club
items.text:
Hana: Are you going to join the drama club?
Leo: I'm not sure. I like acting, but I'm afraid of forgetting my lines.
Hana: Everyone forgets them sometimes. Last year I froze on stage for ten seconds.
Leo: Really? What did you do?
Hana: I waited, smiled, and the other actor helped me. Nobody cared in the end.
Leo: That's comforting. I'll come to the first meeting, at least.
Hana: Great. If you hate it, you can leave. It costs nothing to try.

qs.q: What is Leo's concern?
o: He might forget his lines on stage
He has no time after school
qs.why: 대사를 잊을까 봐 걱정해요.

qs.q: Why does Hana tell the story about last year?
o: To show that she is a better actor
To explain why she left the club
To ask for help with lines
To make Leo feel less worried
qs.why: 자신의 실수를 들려주며 레오를 안심시키려는 의도예요.

qs.q: What does "It costs nothing to try" mean?
o: The club is free for all students this year
Leo has nothing to lose by joining once
Leo should pay the next day
qs.why: 한 번 해보는 데 손해가 없다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What will Leo do?
qs.why: 첫 모임에 가 보겠다고 했어요.

items.q:
Read the message.

"Sorry, my bus broke down. Start dinner without me!"

What can we infer about the writer?
o: The writer will skip the trip
The writer has bought a bus
items.why: 버스가 고장 나서 먼저 먹으라고 했으므로 늦게 도착할 것이에요.

items.q:
Read the sign.

"Please keep your voice down. Others are studying."

Where is this sign most likely found?
items.why: 조용히 하라는 안내이므로 열람실 같은 곳이에요.

items.q:
Read the text.

"The film starts at 7:30. Don't be late. I'm saving you a seat."

What is the writer's purpose?
o: To thank the friend for the film tickets
To remind a friend about the time
items.why: 시간을 상기시키고 자리를 맡아 두겠다는 메시지예요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"It's raining cats and dogs, so I'm staying in."

What does "raining cats and dogs" mean?
items.why: 숙어로 비가 매우 세게 온다는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
Read the note.

"Mom, I fed the dog and took out the trash. Can I go to Dae's house now?"

What does the writer want?
items.why: 할 일을 했으니 친구 집에 가도 되는지 허락을 구하고 있어요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"Wow, you've been waiting an hour? You must be freezing."

What does the speaker assume?
items.why: must be는 강한 추측으로, 오래 기다려 추울 것이라고 짐작해요.

items.q:
Read the ad.

"Lost: a brown wallet near the library. Contains a student card. Reward offered."

What does the writer want readers to do?
o: Return the wallet if they find it
items.why: 분실물을 돌려 달라고 부탁하며 사례를 제안했어요.

items.q:
Read the dialogue.

A: "Could you tell me where the post office is?"

What is the speaker doing?
items.why: Could you tell me ...?는 공손한 질문(문의)이에요.

items.q:
Read the post.

"Finally! After six months of practice, I ran 5 km without stopping. My legs hurt, but I'm smiling."

How does the writer feel?
items.why: 연습 끝에 해낸 성취감과 기쁨이 드러나요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"Their offer sounds too good to be true."

What does the speaker suggest?
o: The offer is the best ever made
The offer may not be honest
items.why: 지나치게 좋은 조건은 의심스럽다는 표현이에요.

items.q:
Read the text.

"Dear neighbors, the elevator will be out of order on Tuesday morning. We apologize for the trouble."

What is the main purpose of this text?
o: To invite people to a party
To ask for a new elevator
items.why: 엘리베이터 사용이 잠시 불가함을 알려요.

items.q:
Read the conversation.

A: "I got the highest score in the class!"
B: "I'm not surprised. You studied day and night."

What does B imply?
o: A copied the answers from the other students
A has earned the result by working hard
A did not study at all
items.why: 밤낮으로 공부했으니 놀랍지 않다는 말은 노력의 결과라는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"He said he would call me back, but it's been a week."

What does the speaker probably feel?
items.why: 일주일이 지나도록 전화가 없어 실망한 마음이에요.

items.q:
Read the label.

"Keep in a cool, dry place. Do not freeze."

What can we infer about the product?
o: It is sold only in summer
Heat or ice could spoil it
items.why: 너무 덥거나 얼어서는 안 된다는 보관 지침이에요.

items.q:
Read the text message.

"Running late! Can you tell the teacher I'll be there in ten minutes?"

What is the sender asking for?
o: A longer lunch break for the class
A message to be passed on
items.why: 선생님께 늦는다고 대신 전해 달라는 부탁이에요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"She gave me a cold look when I sat in her seat."

What does "a cold look" suggest?
o: She was unhappy with the writer
She wanted to say hello to the writer
items.why: cold look은 차갑고 불쾌한 시선을 뜻해요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"The shop windows were dark, and the door was locked. The sign on it said 'Back soon'."

What can we infer?
o: The owner has gone out for a while
The shop is open all night
items.why: '곧 돌아옴'이라는 표지판은 잠시 자리를 비웠다는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
Read the review.

"The food was fine, but we waited an hour for our table. I would not go on a weekend."

What is the writer advising?
o: Book a hotel room near the restaurant
items.why: 주말의 긴 대기를 피하라는 조언이에요.

items.q:
Read the text.

"Mr. Ahn is a man of few words, but when he speaks, everyone listens."

What does "a man of few words" mean?
o: someone who writes books for children
someone who does not talk much
items.why: 말수가 적은 사람을 뜻하는 표현이에요.

items.q:
Read the announcement.

"Passengers are asked to stay in their seats until the plane has come to a complete stop."

Why is this announcement made?
items.why: 완전히 멈추기 전 일어나면 위험하기 때문이에요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"Hana studied all night, yet she looked fresh the next morning."

What does "yet" show?
items.why: yet은 예상과 다른 대조를 나타내요.

items.q:
Read the sentences.

"The path was steep. Joon stopped twice to catch his breath, but he did not turn back."

What does this tell us about Joon?
items.why: 숨이 차도 돌아가지 않았으므로 의지가 강한 사람이에요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"If you have any trouble with the app, please contact our help desk."

What kind of text is this most likely from?
items.why: 앱 문제 시 고객 지원에 연락하라는 안내문이에요.

items.q:
Read the message.

"Thanks for the book, but I already have a copy. I'll give it to my cousin, who loves mysteries."

What is the writer's attitude?
items.why: 고마워하면서도 이미 갖고 있음을 솔직히 말하고 활용 방안을 제시해요.

items.q:
Read the dialogue.

A: "Do you want to come to the movie?"
B: "I'd love to, but I have a test tomorrow."

What does B mean?
o: B will go to the movie gladly
items.why: I'd love to, but ...는 정중한 거절이에요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"The streets were empty, and every shop was closed. It must be a holiday."

What clue leads to this idea?
o: The speaker saw a calendar on the wall
No people or open shops were seen
items.why: 텅 빈 거리와 닫은 가게가 단서가 되어 휴일이라 추측해요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"The new rule was announced on Monday, and by Friday, almost everyone had stopped using plastic bags."

What does this suggest about the rule?
items.why: 일주일 만에 대부분이 비닐봉지를 쓰지 않게 되었으므로 효과적이에요.

items.q:
Read the text.

"Please do not feed the animals. Human food can make them sick."

What reason is given for the rule?
o: Human food can harm the animals
items.why: 사람 음식이 동물을 아프게 할 수 있다고 이유를 밝혔어요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"I'll believe it when I see it."

What is the speaker's attitude?
items.why: 직접 보기 전에는 믿지 못하겠다는 회의적인 태도예요.

items.q:
Read the notice.

"Entry is free for children under six. Adults pay five dollars."

Who would NOT need to pay?
items.why: 6세 미만은 무료이므로 5세 아이는 내지 않아요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"Sora packed an umbrella, a raincoat, and boots, even though the sky was clear."

What can we say about Sora?
items.why: 맑은 날에도 우비를 챙겼으므로 대비하는 성격이에요.

items.q:
Read the note.

"Dear Ms. Lee, I'm sorry I forgot the key. It won't happen again. I'll bring it tomorrow."

What is the writer's purpose?
o: To ask for a new key
To apologize and promise to improve
items.why: 사과와 앞으로의 약속이 담긴 쪽지예요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"He answered the question so quickly that the teacher was surprised."

What does the sentence show?
o: The result of how fast he answered
A wish about the future of the class
items.why: so ... that 구문으로 빠른 대답이 낳은 결과를 나타내요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"The coach praised the team not for winning, but for playing fairly."

What does the coach value most?
items.why: 승리가 아니라 정정당당한 경기를 칭찬했어요.

items.q:
Read the text.

"Our robot vacuum cleans your floors while you are out, so you can come home to a tidy house."

What is the writer trying to do?
o: Teach cleaning skills to the readers
items.why: 제품의 장점을 강조해 구매를 유도하는 광고 문구예요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"Dae-ho put his phone away and looked his grandmother in the eye."

What does this action suggest?
o: He wanted to give her full attention
items.why: 휴대폰을 치우고 눈을 맞추는 행동은 집중해서 듣겠다는 태도예요.

items.q:
Read the sentences.

"The lights went out during the test. For a moment, no one moved. Then the teacher said, 'Stay calm.'"

Why did the teacher say this?
o: To ask someone to turn on the lights
items.why: 정전이 일어나 학생들을 진정시키려는 말이에요.

items.q:
Read the sentence.

"My grandfather's garden is small, but it gives us enough tomatoes for the whole summer."

What does "but" show here?
o: The tomatoes are not as red as they should be
The garden is better than its size suggests
items.why: 작지만 충분하다는 대조를 나타내요.

items.good: He must be tired after the long trip.
items.ko: 긴 여행 뒤라 그는 피곤할 거야.
bad: He must tired after the long trip.
He must is tired after the long trip.
He must to be tired after the long trip.

cz.st: He ___ tired after the long trip.

items.rule: must + be는 현재 사실에 대한 강한 추측('~임에 틀림없다')이에요. must 뒤에는 동사원형이 와요.
items.hint: 확신하는 추측을 나타내는 조동사를 생각해 보세요.

items.good: That can't be Jina's bag because hers is red.
items.ko: 그건 지나의 가방일 리 없어. 그녀의 것은 빨간색이거든.
bad: That can't being Jina's bag because hers is red.
That can't is Jina's bag because hers is red.
That can't to be Jina's bag because hers is red.

cz.st: That ___ Jina's bag because hers is red.

items.rule: can't be는 '~일 리가 없다'는 강한 부정 추측이에요. 뒤에는 동사원형 be를 써요.

items.good: She may have missed the bus, so she is late.
items.ko: 그녀는 버스를 놓쳤을지도 몰라서 늦은 거야.
bad: She may missed the bus, so she is late.
She may has missed the bus, so she is late.
She may have miss the bus, so she is late.

cz.st: She ___ the bus, so she is late.

items.rule: may have + 과거분사는 과거에 대한 약한 추측('~했을지도 모른다')이에요.

items.good: You should have called me before you left.
bad: You should called me before you left.
You should has called me before you left.
You should have call me before you left.
items.rule: should have + 과거분사는 과거에 하지 않은 일에 대한 후회나 비판을 나타내요.
items.hint: 과거에 하지 않은 일에 대한 아쉬움을 나타내요.

items.good: Could you tell me where the station is?
bad: Could you tell me where is the station?
Could you tell me where does the station is?
Could you tell me where the station be?
items.rule: 간접의문문에서는 의문사 뒤에 '주어 + 동사' 순서를 써요. 질문의 어순(is the station)이 아니에요.

items.good: I wonder if she will join our team.
bad: I wonder if will she join our team.
I wonder if she joins will our team.
I wonder whether will she join our team.
items.rule: wonder 뒤의 if는 '~인지 아닌지'를 뜻하며, 이어지는 절은 '주어 + 동사' 어순이에요.

items.good: The movie was so boring that I fell asleep.
items.ko: 그 영화는 너무 지루해서 나는 잠이 들었어.
bad: The movie was so boring what I fell asleep.
The movie was such boring that I fell asleep.
The movie was so boring for I fell asleep.

cz.st: The movie was ___ I fell asleep.

items.rule: so + 형용사 + that ...은 '너무 ~해서 ...하다'라는 결과를 나타내요. such는 뒤에 명사가 와야 해요.

items.good: The test was not only hard but also very long.
items.ko: 시험은 어려울 뿐만 아니라 매우 길었어.
bad: The test was not only hard and also very long.
The test was not only hard but very also long.
The test was only not hard but also very long.

items.good: You had better take an umbrella because it looks like rain.

items.rule: had better 뒤에는 to 없이 동사원형이 와요.
items.hint: 충고하는 표현 뒤의 동사 형태를 확인하세요.

items.good: It seems that he has already finished his homework.

items.rule: It seems that + 주어 + 동사는 '~인 것 같다'는 추측이에요. 주어가 3인칭 단수이므로 has finished로 써요.
